productLossClosed: The shared headless policy identifies only canonical New thread shells with no user message, turn, session, approval, user input, or actionable plan after a 24-hour safety grace.
Lynxtron filters selected stale shells from the first emitted shell and deletes them through the typed thread.delete command.
If a recovered shell was selected, the renderer clears the stale transcript state and selects a remaining canonical thread.
Fresh canonical empty shells retain their direct close control, while normal New Thread entry points continue to reuse one local draft without server persistence.
rootCause: New Thread creation was already local-first, but historical canonical empty shells from older bundles remained in persisted state.
The previous recovery depended on each Sidebar close control being manually tapped, so stale rows could accumulate or remain inaccessible.
safetyBoundary: Automatic recovery runs only on initial or reconnected shell snapshots, not continuously.
The 24-hour grace protects external clients that still use a create-then-start sequence.
Any title, message, turn, session, pending approval, pending user input, actionable plan, archive state, or invalid timestamp prevents automatic deletion.
A failed delete is logged, unhidden, and eligible for a later snapshot retry.
classification.evidenceBoundary: The committed-head run uses a read-only VACUUM copy of ~/.t3-lynxtron and the verifier makes a second disposable copy. The source database was never opened for writing.
